get.description: For load balancers and uptime checks; the only route open without a sign-in.
All sessions, most recently active first.

post.description: Create a session; the provider must be registered.

get.description: One session and its saved transcript; while it runs, `GET .../events` also has the reply in progress.

patch.description:
Switch the session's model or thinking level; the next run uses them. 409 while a run is in progress.

A real switch also leaves a notice in the transcript for the reader; the model never sees it (ADR-008).

post.description: Hide the session from the list; its transcript is kept. 409 while a run is in progress.

Start a run on a new user message and stream its events as SSE.

Each SSE `data` field is one `AgentEvent` as JSON; its `type` names the event.
The server owns the run (ADR-007): closing this stream only stops listening.
Reattach with `GET .../events`; stop the run with `POST .../abort`.

Start a run on the transcript as it is, with no new message: a retry after an error, a stop or a crash.

Streams like `POST .../messages`. 409 if a run is going, 422 if the transcript
is empty or ends with the agent's reply (pi's `agentLoopContinue`).

Summarize the older part of the transcript now (ADR-009); streams the run's events like `.../continue`.

409 if a run is going, 422 if the conversation is too short to compact.

get.description:
Attach to the session's run: a `run_snapshot` first, then live events until the run ends.

With no run in progress, the stream is one snapshot of the saved transcript.

contentSchema.title: Streamitem Watch Session Sessions  Session Id  Events Get

post.description: Queue a message for the model to see after the current turn; it shows up as a `message_end` when it does.
Queue a message for when the run would otherwise stop; the run then goes on with it.
Stop the session's run; finished messages are kept. 409 if nothing is running.

get.description: The catalog; 502 when OpenRouter can't be reached and nothing is cached.
The skills a run started now would see, sorted by name.
One skill, read fresh: its instructions, prompt entry and files.
A text file inside the skill's folder; 404 for anything outside it, missing, binary or over 1 MB.

post.description: Save a server; 409 if its name is taken. Sessions pick it up on their next message.

patch.description: Change a server; its running processes stop now and start again with the new settings when next needed.

delete.description: Delete a server and stop its processes.

post.description:
Start the server once, list its tools and stop it. A failure is a result with `ok: false`, not an HTTP error.

403 while MCP is off, since this runs the server's command on the host.
